deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a Riemann manuscript. It is the first page of an editorial letter dated Aachen, 27 October 1875, addressed to a 'Herr College'. The writer is almost certainly Karl Hattendorff, then at the Aachen Polytechnikum. He had prepared Riemann's posthumous memoir 'Über die Fläche vom kleinsten Inhalt bei gegebener Begrenzung' (Göttingen Abh. 13, 1867). The addressee is very probably Heinrich Weber, who was preparing Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876). The next page supports this: there the writer says he wrote the historical introduction himself after Riemann's death and recounts receiving the manuscript from Riemann in April 1866.

Content of the letter:
- He thanks Weber for his letter of the 21st/24th and agrees that the minimal-surface paper is now in order.
- He accepts Weber's proposed changes.
- On the second change (p. 35) he raises one objection. If the last three lines of §16 are struck, the section never says what A means. One must therefore refer back to where A first appears.
- He proposes this wording: 'Man hat weiter nach den §§ 12 und 13' (one further has, by §§12 and 13):
  du = sqrt( A(c-b)(β+γ)/(2π) ) · (t-a)^{1/2} dt / ((t-b)(t-c)),
  'or, if one assumes c - b = 2π/A':
  du = (t-a)^{1/2} dt / ((t-b)(t-c)) · sqrt(β+γ).

Mathematics:
- t is the auxiliary complex variable on the half-plane onto which Riemann maps the surface.
- u is one of the Riemann/Weierstrass-type functions whose differential is built algebraically in t. Its branch point is at a, and its simple poles at b and c produce logarithmic terms, corresponding to boundary components or ends at infinity.
- A, β, γ are constants of the example in §16 (A introduced earlier, β+γ an angle/parameter sum).
- The only step is a normalization. Choosing the free scale so that c - b = 2π/A makes A(c-b)/(2π) = 1, so the prefactor reduces to sqrt(β+γ). This step is trivially correct (taking the positive square root throughout).

The purpose is purely editorial: to keep the definition of A traceable once a passage is deleted.
errors: No mathematical errors. The normalization c - b = 2π/A correctly reduces sqrt(A(c-b)(β+γ)/(2π)) to sqrt(β+γ).
Attribution caution: this page is by the editor (very likely Hattendorff), not by Riemann. It should not be credited to Riemann as an original derivation.

results.what: Normalization of the constant in the differential du = C·(t-a)^{1/2} dt/((t-b)(t-c)) for an example in Riemann's minimal-surface memoir (§16 of the Werke version), choosing c-b = 2π/A
results.modern_name: Scale normalization in a Weierstrass/Schwarz–Christoffel-type representation of a minimal surface
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (memoir publ. 1867, ed. Hattendorff); editorial text for the Werke by Hattendorff/Weber 1875-76

results.what: Editorial correspondence about revising the published text (striking three lines of §16, cross-reference to the first occurrence of A)
results.modern_name: Editorial history of Riemann's Gesammelte Werke

deep.surprise_reason: This is an 1875 editorial letter about an already published Riemann paper. Its only computation is a trivial constant normalization. It has archival interest for the editing history of the Werke but no new mathematics.

checkable.sympy: A,b,beta,gamma=symbols('A b beta gamma',positive=True); c=b+2*pi/A; simplify(sqrt(A*(c-b)*(beta+gamma)/(2*pi)) - sqrt(beta+gamma)) == 0
checkable.asserts: With c-b = 2π/A the prefactor reduces to sqrt(β+γ)

checkable.sympy: t,a,b,c=symbols('t a b c'); residue(sqrt(t-a)/((t-b)*(t-c)), t, b) - sqrt(b-a)/(b-c)
checkable.asserts: Residue of the integrand at t=b is sqrt(b-a)/(b-c), giving logarithmic behaviour of u (should simplify to 0)

transcription_corrections: Transcription matches the image essentially. 'Octbr' is written 'Octbr' with superscript abbreviation; 'Hochgeehrter Herr College!' is correct.
In the formulas the exponent 1/2 on (t-a) is written as a superscript fraction, consistent with the transcription.
